nodes.label: Migration next steps
nodes.rationale: Progression after setup. When this note was written, Phase 2 implementation had landed and Phase 3 endpoint code was underway, with tests and parity still open.

nodes.label: Phase 2: Auth, OTP, accounts
nodes.source_location: 1. Phase 2: Auth, OTP, accounts (implementation landed; parity gate pending)
nodes.rationale: Port SEP-10 challenge and token, Sep10JwtGuard, PIN lockout with the legacy Redis keys and TTLs, OTP send and verify including TextBee and test-mode rules, register and user lookup, then the signup security tests under Jest. The gate is typecheck, module tests, and contract parity against legacy.

nodes.label: Phase 3: Wallet, transactions, settlements
nodes.rationale: Implementation started 2026-10-29. Wallet, transfer confirmation, and signed settlement services existed, and 16 focused unit tests passed. Recipient-registry cases and request/response parity were still open. No auth decision should be made silently; deviations go in the migration plan decision log.

nodes.label: Phase 4: Engine / Soroban
nodes.rationale: Highest-risk phase. Port concurrency, retry-classifier, and transaction-manager tests first, then Ed25519SignatureGuard and the engine routes, and convert settle to a BullMQ processor while keeping HTTP compatibility for external callers. The gate is matching simulation and submission plus concurrency-tested retries, queues, and locks.

nodes.label: Phase 5: SMS, queue, voucher security
nodes.source_location: 4. Phase 5: SMS, queue, voucher security (implementation underway)
nodes.rationale: Port the TextBee client with fallback and signature guard, the dispatch queue, the inbound webhook, and offline voucher verification, plus sms-security, sms-delivery, and offline-voucher-security tests. Close the phase only after webhook signatures, fallback, and rate limits are verified.

nodes.label: Phase 6: Anchor / SEP-24
nodes.source_location: 5. Phase 6: Anchor / SEP-24 and web pages
nodes.rationale: Port anchor endpoints and ramp-security tests. The interactive flow, including interactive JWT security, must work against the hosted Nest backend before cutover.

nodes.label: Phase 7: Demo, friendbot, scripts
nodes.rationale: Port demo modules behind DEMO_ENABLED, add friendbot with testnet-only guards, and port operational scripts. Demo-only flows stay disabled unless explicitly enabled, including in production.

nodes.label: Phase 8: Deploy and cutover
nodes.rationale: Choose a long-running host, prove staging with legacy-versus-Nest checks, then point mobile at the new base URL. Keep the Vercel legacy deployment alive until cutover is stable and the rollback path is validated.

nodes.label: Migration guardrails
nodes.rationale: Keep apps/_legacy/backend read-only and copy logic instead of importing it. Do not change the Prisma schema unless the decision log says so. Run a legacy-versus-Nest parity check before marking an endpoint complete, and require typecheck, test, build, and relevant e2e before the next phase.

nodes.label: Start with Phase 2
nodes.rationale: Start with auth, OTP, and accounts because bootstrap is already in place and the main risks are route parity and JWT/OTP behavior. That continues the migration without destabilizing the foundation.

nodes.label: Anchor web pages
nodes.source_location: 5. Phase 6: Anchor / SEP-24 and web pages
nodes.rationale: Decide whether Nest server-rendered views or a separate small web app serves pages during migration. SEP-24 deposit and withdraw, privacy policy, delete account, and demo pages if needed must exist before cutover.

nodes.label: DEMO_ENABLED
nodes.rationale: Demo-only flows stay disabled unless explicitly enabled, so they cannot turn on by accident in production.

nodes.label: Vercel legacy deployment
nodes.rationale: Keep the Vercel legacy deployment alive until a stable cutover is confirmed.
